title: Renovate has zero coverage for home/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl
description: renovate.json5's mise manager (line 30-34) is scoped to managerFilePatterns: ['/^mise\.toml$/'] -- the root repo-tooling file only (bats/gitleaks/shellcheck/etc). It does not cover home/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl, the actual user dev-environment config with 100+ pinned tool versions (aqua/github/npm/pipx-backed CLIs, language servers, MCP servers). docs/renovate.md explicitly documents 5 custom managers that should cover this file -- 'Custom Managers' items 2-5 (aqua-prefixed, github-prefixed, npm-prefixed, pipx-prefixed tools in mise TOML) plus the base mise manager -- with worked examples like 'aqua:mikefarah/yq' and 'npm:@anthropic-ai/claude-code'. None of these customManagers actually exist in renovate.json5 (verified: zero matches for aqua:/github:/npm:/pipx: patterns in the file's customManagers block). Even if they did exist, the documented path 'home/dot_config/mise/config.toml' is itself wrong -- the real file is config.toml.tmpl (a Chezmoi template), so a manager targeting the undotted name would never match the real file either way. Net effect: every version pin in this large, security/reproducibility-relevant file (mise.lock's source of truth) gets zero automated Renovate PRs today, contradicting docs/renovate.md, docs/package-management.md's Quick Reference table (marks this file 'Yes' for Renovate coverage), and docs/adrs/0003-mise-config-plus-lockfile.md's stated model. Fix: add the 4 missing aqua/github/npm/pipx customManagers scoped to the correct .tmpl path (and fix the base mise manager's pattern to also include it), matching the docs' own worked examples -- this is squarely Package Manager subagent / Renovate config territory per AGENTS.md.

title: install: cosign signature verification for chezmoi download is broken (upstream moved to Sigstore bundles)
description: ./install downloads chezmoi from GitHub releases (home/../install lines ~813-869) when apt/brew can't provide it. With the default VERIFY_SIGNATURES=true, it downloads chezmoi_<version>_checksums.txt.sig and chezmoi_cosign.pub and runs 'cosign verify-blob --signature ... --key ...'. As of chezmoi v2.71.1, upstream no longer publishes a .sig/.pub pair for checksums.txt -- confirmed via the GitHub Releases API, the actual assets are chezmoi_<version>_checksums.txt.sigstore.json (a Sigstore bundle) plus per-artifact .sbom.json files. The old .sig filename now 404s every time, so any fresh install path that can't satisfy chezmoi via apt/brew (e.g. Debian/Ubuntu, which doesn't package chezmoi at all, including inside a plain container) fails outright with VERIFY_SIGNATURES=true. sha256 checksum verification (verify_checksum, unconditional) still runs fine and is unaffected -- only the extra cosign signature-of-the-checksums-file step is broken. Likely also affects CI's cold-start.yml/ci.yml on ubuntu-24.04 runners, since bootstrap-dotfiles/action.yml never sets VERIFY_SIGNATURES=false and apt has no chezmoi package there either -- worth confirming whether CI is currently green only by luck (e.g. a cached/pre-installed chezmoi) or is quietly broken too. Fix should update install's cosign invocation to verify the .sigstore.json bundle (Sigstore keyless verification: cosign verify-blob --bundle chezmoi_<version>_checksums.txt.sigstore.json --certificate-identity-regexp ... --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, matching whatever identity/issuer chezmoi's release workflow actually uses) instead of the retired detached-signature scheme. Found while building a new root Dockerfile (dotfiles-au4) -- worked around there by pinning VERIFY_SIGNATURES=false with a comment pointing at this issue, since fixing the verification scheme itself is out of scope for that change.

title: tmux-plugins.yaml jsonata Renovate manager queries fields that don't exist in the file
description: renovate.json5's jsonata customManager for tmux plugins (~line 182-192) uses the query: tmuxPlugins.{ "depName": repo, "currentValue": ref, "currentDigest": commit } against home/.chezmoidata/tmux-plugins.yaml. But that file's actual structure (confirmed by reading it) has root key tmux_plugins (snake_case, not tmuxPlugins) containing an extras array of objects shaped { path, type, url, revision } -- none of repo/ref/commit exist anywhere in the file. The jsonata query evaluates to an empty result, so Renovate silently never checks the three pinned tmux plugin revisions (tmux-sensible, tmux-powerline, tmux-prefix-highlight) for updates, despite docs/adrs/0002-tmux-plugins-via-chezmoi-externals.md explicitly claiming Renovate 'can target stable file + field shapes in YAML for digest/SHA bumps' for this exact file. Fix: correct the jsonata query to match the real shape, e.g. tmux_plugins.extras.{ "depName": url, "currentDigest": revision } (adjusting depName extraction since url is a full git URL, not an owner/repo shorthand like the other jsonata/regex managers use).

title: 4 Renovate customManagers target a nonexistent home/.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl path
description:
renovate.json5 has 4 customManagers (catppuccin/ghostty ~line 117, ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh ~130, zsh-autosuggestions ~143, zsh-syntax-highlighting ~156) all scoped to managerFilePatterns: ['/^home/\.chezmoiexternal\.toml\.tmpl$/'] -- a singular file that no longer exists. Externals were split into home/.chezmoiexternals/ (plural directory: fish.toml.tmpl, ghostty.toml, sketchybar-*.toml.tmpl, tmux.toml.tmpl, zsh.toml.tmpl). The sketchybar-related customManagers were correctly updated to this new layout (~line 87, ~170); these 4 were not. They can never match any file, so these 4 pins are never checked for updates.

Fixing the path alone isn't enough for 3 of the 4: home/.chezmoiexternals/zsh.toml.tmpl currently pins ohmyzsh, zsh-autosuggestions, and zsh-syntax-highlighting to literal 'archive/master.tar.gz' URLs -- a floating branch reference, not a commit SHA -- so even a corrected regex (which expects a 7-40 char hex digest) wouldn't match. This also contradicts docs/renovate.md's 'All externals pinned to commit SHAs' claim and this repo's own stated pinning policy (AGENTS.md / Package Manager subagent: 'pin tarball to commit SHA'). The 4th, home/.chezmoiexternals/ghostty.toml, is already correctly pinned to a commit SHA (5a58926563ddacbde4a12b4a347464c2c6945393) -- only its manager's file path needs fixing.

Fix: update all 4 managers' managerFilePatterns to the correct plural-directory paths, and separately pin the 3 zsh-related externals to commit SHAs (matching ghostty.toml's existing pattern) so the corrected regex actually has something to match.

title: packages.yaml: .packages.linux has no apt list, only dnf — Debian/Ubuntu users get zero packages from run_onchange_install-packages-linux.sh
description: home/.chezmoidata/packages.yaml defines packages.linux.dnf (ca-certificates, gh, git, git-lfs, htop, neovim, tmux, util-linux-user, zsh) but has no packages.linux.apt list at all. home/.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_install-packages-linux.sh.tmpl templates '(index .packages.linux "apt")' with a 'default list' fallback, so on any apt-based system (Debian, Ubuntu, WSL Ubuntu, containers) the apt branch runs apt-get install -y with an empty package list -- meaning gh/git-lfs/htop/neovim/tmux/util-linux-user/jq never get installed via this path on apt systems today, bare metal or container. Discovered while building the new Dockerfile (dotfiles-au4): jq specifically caused a hard failure there (bin/sync-claude-extras exits 1 without it once claude is installed), worked around locally by adding jq directly to the Dockerfile's own apt-get install line since the container guard in that script assumes packages are already baked into the image. A proper fix should add a packages.linux.apt list mirroring the dnf one (package names may differ slightly, e.g. util-linux-user has no direct apt equivalent -- verify per package) so bare-metal Debian/Ubuntu users aren't silently missing these tools too.

title: install: install_chezmoi's own PATH check runs before add_to_path, always fails on GitHub-fallback path in non-interactive shells
description: install_chezmoi() (install lines ~887-939) downloads+installs chezmoi to $BIN_DIR via download_chezmoi(), then immediately checks 'command -v chezmoi' (line ~934) to verify success. But $BIN_DIR (default ~/.local/bin) is only added to PATH by add_to_path(), which main() doesn't call until line ~1014 -- AFTER run_logged_step chezmoi (line ~1012) has already returned. Since install_chezmoi runs inside run_logged_step's subshell, its own command -v check always runs before PATH has been updated, so it always fails whenever chezmoi is installed via the GitHub-release fallback (i.e. whenever apt/brew can't provide chezmoi, e.g. on Debian/Ubuntu, which doesn't package chezmoi at all). This is masked on interactive shells where ~/.local/bin is typically already on PATH via ~/.profile/~/.zprofile before ./install even runs, but is a hard, deterministic failure in any non-interactive context that doesn't pre-seed PATH (confirmed in a fresh container). Interestingly, install_chezmoi's own check (lines 933-938, 'chezmoi installation failed - binary not found in PATH', hard exit 1) is redundant with -- and less robust than -- the proper fallback resolution main() already does 80 lines later (lines ~1016-1029: probes command -v, falls back to checking /chezmoi and other absolute-path candidates directly, regardless of PATH). Fix: either remove/relax install_chezmoi's premature command -v check (checking file existence at /chezmoi instead, since download_chezmoi already mv+chmod's it unconditionally), or call add_to_path earlier before this check runs. Found and worked around at the Dockerfile level (dotfiles-au4) by pre-seeding ENV PATH to include the container user's ~/.local/bin before running ./install -- that's a reasonable container-specific accommodation, but the underlying ordering bug affects any non-interactive ./install invocation, not just containers.

title: Containerize dotfiles dev environment with a Dockerfile
description: Add a Dockerfile (and likely docker-compose or devcontainer config) so the dotfiles repo can be built into a container image, letting anyone spin up a fully-configured dev environment without running ./install on bare metal. Should reuse the existing chezmoi-based install flow rather than duplicating package lists.
acceptance_criteria: A Dockerfile exists at the repo root (or docker/ dir) that: 1) builds an image with mise + chezmoi + the tools this repo installs, 2) applies the chezmoi source so the resulting ~ matches what's committed, 3) is documented in README.md with build/run instructions. CI or a manual smoke test confirms the image builds and a shell inside it reflects the dotfiles config.
notes: Fully validated end to end: docker build completes cleanly (real chezmoi version resolves via the install fix, no hang), docker run -it drops into a working zsh shell with correct git identity from build args, and 'bin/setup; bin/test' passes all 73 bats tests inside the built image. hk check shows no new lint regressions (shellcheck/markdownlint/gitleaks/jq all clean on touched files; the one ghalint failure on cold-start.yml predates this work). Not verified: opening via VS Code/Cursor 'Reopen in Container' interactively (devcontainer.json is valid JSON and follows the spec, but wasn't exercised in an actual editor), and the new docker.yml workflow going green on a real PR (can't push from here). Both are reasonable to confirm once this lands.
close_reason: Dockerfile + .devcontainer/devcontainer.json + docker.yml CI job implemented and validated (build + full test suite pass). Four unrelated pre-existing bugs found along the way tracked separately: dotfiles-xeo, dotfiles-b73, dotfiles-gyp, dotfiles-f14.

title: docs/tmux.md and ADR-0002 describe the removed gpakosz/.tmux architecture
description:
docs/tmux.md (the whole file) documents tmux as built on gpakosz/.tmux vendored via a Chezmoi external at .tmux (type = git-repo), with ~/.tmux.conf symlinked into it, home/dot_tmux.conf.local for overrides, and TPM plugin support. None of this exists anymore: home/dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf line 2 states outright 'Replaces gpakosz/.tmux framework with explicit settings + tmux-sensible', there is no .tmux external anywhere in home/.chezmoiexternals/, and there is no dot_tmux.conf.local file. Plugins are now tmux-sensible/tmux-powerline/tmux-prefix-highlight loaded via run-shell, declared in home/.chezmoidata/tmux-plugins.yaml and fetched as individual git-repo externals (home/.chezmoiexternals/tmux.toml.tmpl).

docs/adrs/0002-tmux-plugins-via-chezmoi-externals.md's context section rests on the same now-false premise ('This repo already vendors the base gpakosz/.tmux layout...') and is marked status: accepted with no superseded note, even though the architecture it's reasoning about no longer exists.

This is a real risk for both humans and coding agents: docs/tmux.md is the doc AGENTS.md-adjacent tooling would point someone to for tmux config, and it currently describes files/behavior (dot_tmux.conf.local, the .tmux external, TPM) that don't exist, which would send anyone troubleshooting tmux down a dead end. Fix: rewrite docs/tmux.md to describe the current tmux-sensible + individually-pinned-plugin architecture, and add a superseded/updated note to ADR-0002's context (or a new ADR) reflecting the gpakosz removal.

title: bin/setup's mise install exit code is unreliable as a gate before bin/test
description: bin/setup runs 'exec mise install' from the repo root, which mise resolves against BOTH the local root mise.toml (bats-core, gitleaks, shellcheck, etc -- the actual test/lint dependencies) AND the merged global user config (home/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl's much larger tool list). If any tool in that merged set fails -- observed in a container: aqua:o2sh/onefetch@latest ('unsupported env: linux/arm64', not a real bug, just missing on that one arch) and npm:@google/gemini-cli@latest ('no version of @google/gemini-cli matches 0.0.8999999999999999', a broken/malformed npm-published version, arch-independent) -- mise install exits 1 overall, even though the tools actually needed (bats-core included) installed successfully and bin/test passes all 73 tests cleanly when run anyway. AGENTS.md documents the workflow as 'Run via ./bin/test after ./bin/setup', which reads naturally as bin/setup && bin/test -- but chaining with && makes bin/test never run whenever any unrelated global-config tool is broken. Discovered while validating the new Dockerfile/docker.yml (dotfiles-au4); worked around there by not chaining with &&. Two independent angles worth considering: (1) gemini-cli's broken npm version specifically -- verify whether it's a transient upstream npm state or a stale/wrong version pin in home/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl; (2) more generally, bin/setup's exit code probably shouldn't gate bin/test at all, or bin/test's own docs/CI usage should stop chaining them with &&.
